newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end up in correction, outlook lower.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end up in correction, outlook lower.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled higher in thin trade but analysts said the near-term outlook for prices remains negative.
The benchmark September contract closed 0.75 cent firmer at 75.70 cents per lb, having ranged from 75.90 to 74.80 cents. The rest of the board finished up 0.30 to 0.70 cent.
An estimated 1,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Friday's official 1,335 lots.
Near-term support in September remained at the contract low of 73.60 cents, followed by 72.00 cents, market analysts said.
"Everyone is on both sides of the market excluding the funds," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said. "The only thing that could spark this market is a hurricane."
The market also awaits an estimate of the 1997/98 crop by Citrus Consulting International, a private firm. The estimate, typically the first of the new season, will be released August 14.
